map.Low-risk investments always pay the high: Safe investments like savings accounts pay the best returns
map.Risk and return are not related to each: Risk affects possible losses but has no link to expected returns
map.Higher returns always come with lower ri: Investments with higher returns tend to be safer than others

ww.Safe investments like savings accounts p: Safe investments such as savings accounts usually pay lower returns; the largest potential gains come from riskier assets like stocks, which is the core of the risk-return tradeoff.
ww.Risk affects possible losses but has no: Risk and expected return are linked; investors ask for a higher possible payoff to accept more risk, so treating them as separate ideas misses the tradeoff.
ww.Investments with higher returns tend to: Higher potential returns usually come with more risk, not less; if high returns were safe, buyers would rush in and prices would rise until the extra return disappeared.

map.Secret, Modest, Automatic, Random and Te: Simple, Meaningful, Ambitious, Rewarding and Tangible
map.Simple, Memorable, Awesome, Rare and Tou: Specific, Motivating, Ambitious, Rigid and Traditional
map.Safe, Mild, Average, Reliable and Typica: Strategic, Meaningful, Aggressive, Rewarding and Timeless

ww.Simple, Meaningful, Ambitious, Rewarding: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound; the words Simple, Meaningful, Ambitious, Rewarding and Tangible are not the framework, even though they sound positive.
ww.Specific, Motivating, Ambitious, Rigid a: Only the first word matches; SMART continues with Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound, so a goal described as motivating, ambitious, rigid and traditional does not fit the framework.
ww.Strategic, Meaningful, Aggressive, Rewar: SMART letters stand for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound; a timeless goal has no deadline, which goes against the time-bound part of the framework.

map.A want is always required by law to buy: A want is a basic item; a need is a luxury item
map.A need can only be bought with a credit: A need is bought with credit; a want is bought with cash

ww.A want is a basic item; a need is a luxu: Needs such as food, housing and health care are basic and essential, while wants are luxuries, so this description swaps the two ideas around.
ww.A need is bought with credit; a want is: Payment method does not decide whether something is a need or a want; the difference is whether the item is essential to live and work, however it is paid for.

map.A cost that is always equal to income fo: A cost that you pay with a credit card instead of cash
map.A cost that is exactly the same every mo: A cost that stays the same each month, such as rent
map.A cost that is paid only once in a lifet: Money set aside each month for the future, such as retirement

ww.A cost that you pay with a credit card i: A variable expense is defined by an amount that changes from month to month, not by the payment method, since rent or groceries can be paid by card or cash.
ww.A cost that stays the same each month, s: A cost that stays the same each month is a fixed expense; variable expenses are the ones whose amounts rise and fall, such as entertainment or dining out.
ww.Money set aside each month for the futur: Money set aside for the future is saving, not an expense; a variable expense is spending that changes in amount from month to month, like entertainment.

map.A company that only sells insurance plan: A company that pools premiums to cover losses
map.A store that sells only gold and jewelry: A firm that trades stocks and bonds for clients

ww.A company that pools premiums to cover l: A company that collects premiums and pays out claims is an insurer; a bank instead takes deposits, makes loans and offers payment services.
ww.A firm that trades stocks and bonds for: A firm that trades stocks and bonds for clients is a brokerage; a bank takes deposits from savers and lends that money to borrowers.

map.A savings account with unlimited free wi: A savings account that lets you withdraw money freely
map.A stock that pays dividends every quarte: A share of company ownership that pays a quarterly dividend

ww.A savings account that lets you withdraw: A savings account allows flexible withdrawals, while a CD locks the money for a fixed term and usually charges a penalty for taking it out early.
ww.A share of company ownership that pays a: A share of ownership that pays dividends is a stock; a CD is a bank deposit that earns fixed interest over a set term and gives no ownership.

map.A loan with no fees and no interest at a: A low-rate loan repaid over several years
map.A government grant that never needs repa: A bonus your employer pays out on payday

ww.A low-rate loan repaid over several year: Payday loans are small, short-term and costly, due on the next payday; a low-rate loan with years to repay describes an installment loan instead.
ww.A bonus your employer pays out on payday: A bonus from an employer is earned pay that never has to be repaid; a payday loan is borrowed money that must be repaid with fees.

map.Only gold and silver bars in a vault: Anything that people choose to save

ww.Anything backed by gold reserves: Money does not need gold backing; modern currencies are accepted because people trust and use them, and economists define money by its function as accepted payment.
ww.Anything that earns steady interest: Earning interest is not what makes something money; cash earns none, yet it is money because people widely accept it as payment for goods and services.
ww.Anything that people choose to save: Saving something does not make it money; economists define money by its use as a medium of exchange that sellers will accept in payment.

map.Interest that changes with the market ev: Interest that adjusts when market rates change
map.Interest that is paid only at the time o: Interest that is paid by the government on savings

ww.Interest that adjusts when market rates: Interest that adjusts with market rates describes a variable rate; simple interest is a calculation method that uses the original principal and stays the same each period.
ww.Interest that is paid by the government: Simple interest is a way of calculating interest on principal, and it can be paid by any lender or bank, not specifically by the government.

map.Interest that is paid out and never adde: Interest paid out to the holder and not kept in the account
map.Interest calculated only on the original: Interest calculated on the original amount borrowed each year
map.Interest that decreases every year until: Interest that shrinks as the principal gets paid down

ww.Interest paid out to the holder and not: Paying interest out without adding it to the balance is how simple interest behaves; compound interest stays in the account and then earns interest of its own.
ww.Interest calculated on the original amou: Interest figured on just the original amount is simple interest, whereas compound interest also applies to interest already added in earlier periods.
ww.Interest that shrinks as the principal g: Interest that shrinks as a loan balance falls describes an amortizing loan; compound interest grows because earned interest is added to the balance and earns more.

map.A rate that is always zero for every bor: A rate that drops each year as the balance falls
map.A rate that only applies in the first mo: A rate that applies to a short introductory period

ww.A rate that drops each year as the balan: A fixed rate does not fall as the balance falls; it stays the same for the whole loan term, which makes payments predictable.
ww.A rate that applies to a short introduct: A rate that lasts for a short introductory period is a teaser rate that later changes; a fixed rate stays unchanged for the full loan term.

map.A number that shows how much money someo: A number that shows the total balance a person owes on loans
map.A number that shows how many cards someo: A number that shows how many times a person applied for credit

ww.A number that shows the total balance a: A credit score estimates how likely someone is to repay debts; it is not a total of what is owed, though balances are one factor in the calculation.
ww.A number that shows how many times a per: The number of credit applications is a small input called inquiries; the score itself combines payment history, balances and other factors to estimate repayment risk.

map.Higher returns always come with lower ri: Lower-risk investments tend to offer the highest potential returns
map.Returns are guaranteed for risky assets: Risky assets are insured, so their returns are protected

ww.Lower-risk investments tend to offer the: Low-risk investments such as savings accounts offer lower returns; the chance of higher returns usually requires taking more risk, so this reverses the relationship.
ww.Risky assets are insured, so their retur: Risky assets such as stocks are not insured against market losses; their values can fall, which is exactly why they are called risky.

map.Their value never changes over any perio: Their value is set daily by the Federal Reserve
map.They are always backed by gold and silve: They are printed by the Treasury in limited amounts
map.They are guaranteed by the government ag: They are covered by FDIC insurance up to a limit

ww.Their value is set daily by the Federal: No central bank sets cryptocurrency prices; they move with trading demand, which is why values can swing sharply and make them risky for savings.
ww.They are printed by the Treasury in limi: Treasury does not print cryptocurrency; it is created by software networks, and its value rests on demand and trust, which adds risk for savers.
ww.They are covered by FDIC insurance up to: Cryptocurrency holdings are not covered by FDIC insurance, so if the price drops or an exchange fails, the saver can lose the money.

map.An asset that never changes value over t: An asset that holds steady value, such as a savings balance
map.An asset that gains value over time, wit: An asset that rises in value over time, such as land

ww.An asset that holds steady value, such a: An asset that holds steady value does not depreciate; depreciation means a decline in value from age, wear or obsolescence, as with a new car.
ww.An asset that rises in value over time,: An asset that rises in value over time is an appreciating asset, which is the opposite of a depreciating asset that loses value.

map.To guarantee that you will never have an: To pay for damage caused by theft, fire or storms
map.To pay for your own car repairs only, af: To repair your own car after a crash you cause

ww.To pay for damage caused by theft, fire: Damage from theft, fire or storms is handled by comprehensive coverage; liability insurance pays for injuries and property damage you cause to other people.
ww.To repair your own car after a crash you: Repairing your own car is the job of collision coverage; liability insurance pays for harm you cause to other people and their property.

map.Damage to other people's cars only: Medical bills for passengers in your car
map.Damage from theft only to a car: Damage from hail, fire or flooding

ww.Medical bills for passengers in your car: Medical bills for passengers fall under medical payments or injury coverage; collision coverage pays to repair or replace your own car after an accident.
ww.Damage from hail, fire or flooding: Damage from hail, fire or flooding is covered by comprehensive coverage; collision pays for damage from crashes with other vehicles or objects.

map.Every natural disaster, even floods and: Flood and earthquake damage to the house
map.Only the land under the home and nothing: Routine upkeep like repainting and lawn care
map.Only the mortgage payments made each mon: Mortgage payments if the owner loses a job

ww.Flood and earthquake damage to the house: Flood and earthquake damage are excluded from standard homeowners policies and need separate coverage, so this does not describe what a typical policy covers.
ww.Routine upkeep like repainting and lawn: Routine upkeep is the owner's responsibility; homeowners insurance pays for sudden losses such as fire or theft, not regular maintenance.
ww.Mortgage payments if the owner loses a j: Homeowners insurance protects the property and liability; it does not make mortgage payments if the owner loses a job, which would need a different product.

map.The yearly total you pay for insurance,: The monthly amount you pay to keep your insurance policy active
map.The portion of the cost that the insurer: The amount you must pay before your insurance starts to pay

ww.The monthly amount you pay to keep your: The monthly amount paid to keep a policy active is the premium; a copay is a separate fixed fee paid when you receive a service.
ww.The amount you must pay before your insu: The amount paid before coverage begins is a deductible; a copay is a fixed fee paid for a covered service, such as a doctor visit.

map.Both cover only one year and then must b: Term builds cash value you can borrow against; whole life does not
map.Term covers a lifetime; whole life cover: Term covers a lifetime; whole life covers a set period of years
map.Neither pays a death benefit to anyone a: Both pay the death benefit to the owner while the insured is alive

ww.Term builds cash value you can borrow ag: Whole life is the policy that builds cash value you can borrow against; term insurance is pure protection for a set period and builds none.
ww.Term covers a lifetime; whole life cover: This swaps the two products; term insurance covers a set number of years, while whole life covers the insured for life and builds cash value.
ww.Both pay the death benefit to the owner: A death benefit is paid to the beneficiary after the insured dies, not to the owner during life, and both term and whole life pay it.

map.Coverage for rain damage only, from stor: Coverage for storm damage to a home
map.Coverage for cars only, up to a certain: Coverage for your medical bills after illness

ww.Coverage for storm damage to a home: Storm damage to a home falls under homeowners insurance; an umbrella policy adds extra liability protection above the limits of other policies.
ww.Coverage for jewelry and valuables: Coverage for jewelry and valuables is personal property insurance; an umbrella policy provides extra liability coverage once other policy limits are used up.
ww.Coverage for your medical bills after il: Medical bills are paid by health insurance; an umbrella policy is extra liability coverage that protects assets from large lawsuits above other limits.

map.Withdrawals are always allowed without p: You must begin taking required withdrawals at age 73
map.It is available only to employers and no: It is a plan offered by an employer with a company match

ww.You must begin taking required withdrawa: Roth IRAs have no required withdrawals during the owner's life; the main feature is after-tax contributions with tax-free qualified withdrawals in retirement.
ww.It is a plan offered by an employer with: A Roth IRA is opened by an individual with earned income, not offered through an employer, and there is no company match on contributions.

map.There are no limits on contributions to: Contributions are limited to the amount your employer matches
map.It pays a guaranteed return of ten perce: It pays a fixed interest rate set by the federal government

ww.Contributions are limited to the amount: IRA contribution limits are set yearly by law and are not tied to an employer match, which is a feature of workplace plans like a 401(k).
ww.It pays a fixed interest rate set by the: An IRA is an account type, not an investment with a set rate; returns depend on what the saver invests in, and the government sets no rate.

map.A plan that pays no benefit to any of it: A plan that pays a benefit based on salary and years worked
map.A plan that only the government funds fo: A savings plan in which the government makes the deposits
map.A plan where the employer guarantees a f: A health plan that covers medical costs after retirement

ww.A plan that pays a benefit based on sala: A benefit based on salary and years of service describes a defined benefit pension; in a defined contribution plan the contribution is set and the payout varies.
ww.A savings plan in which the government m: Defined contribution plans such as a 401(k) are funded by the worker and often the employer, not by the government making all deposits.
ww.A health plan that covers medical costs: Covering medical costs in retirement is a health benefit, not a retirement savings plan; a defined contribution plan sets contributions and the payout depends on investments.

map.An account that guarantees a fixed retur: An account that earns interest from deposits
map.An account used only to pay monthly bill: An account for writing checks to pay bills

ww.An account that earns interest from depo: An account that earns interest on deposits describes a savings account; a brokerage account is used to hold and trade investments such as stocks and funds.
ww.An account for writing checks to pay bil: Writing checks and paying bills is what a checking account is for; a brokerage account is built to buy and sell investments.

map.An order that triggers only if a price f: An order that becomes active once the price falls to a set level
map.An order to buy only at a set price or l: An order to buy or sell at a price you name or better

ww.An order that becomes active once the pr: That describes a stop order, which waits for a trigger price; a market order has no trigger and executes right away at the best available price.
ww.An order to buy or sell at a price you n: Naming a price you will accept is a limit order; a market order does not wait for a price and takes the best current price.

map.Only when you are applying for a loan or: Once a year, when you do your taxes
map.Never, because banks are always correct: Just when a charge looks unusually large
map.Only once every ten years, if at all, on: Once a decade when you clean out your files

ww.Once a year, when you do your taxes: Checking just once a year lets errors and fraud sit unnoticed for months and may miss dispute deadlines; statements should be reviewed regularly, often monthly.
ww.Just when a charge looks unusually large: Waiting for a large charge lets small fraudulent or mistaken charges go unnoticed; reviewing every statement regularly catches both big and small problems early.
ww.Once a decade when you clean out your fi: Waiting a decade would let fraud and errors pile up and miss dispute deadlines; statements should be reviewed regularly to catch problems promptly.

map.Pay for overtime only, not regular hours: Pay earned from a second job
map.Pay received only from tips and gratuiti: Base salary excluding bonuses and commissions

ww.Pay earned from a second job: Gross pay is the combined total of all earnings from every source before deductions, not just pay from one extra job.
ww.Base salary excluding bonuses and commis: Gross pay includes bonuses and commissions along with base salary, so leaving them out understates the total earned before taxes and deductions.

map.Needs are always luxury items for the ri: Needs are optional items; wants are required to live
map.Wants are always cheaper than needs in a: Wants are bought with cash; needs are bought on credit
map.There is no difference between them at a: Both words mean items that a shopper must buy

ww.Needs are optional items; wants are requ: This reverses the meanings; needs such as food and housing are required to live, while wants are optional items that are nice to have.
ww.Wants are bought with cash; needs are bo: The way something is paid for does not separate wants from needs; the difference is whether the item is essential or just nice to have.
ww.Both words mean items that a shopper mus: Wants are optional, so a shopper does not have to buy them; separating needs from wants is a key step in good budgeting.

map.A loan only for businesses: A loan from a family member
map.A loan guaranteed by luck: A loan with no credit check

ww.A loan from a family member: A loan from a relative has no required collateral; a secured loan is defined by the asset the lender can claim if the borrower stops paying.
ww.A loan with no credit check: Skipping a credit check does not make a loan secured; a secured loan is backed by collateral such as a car or house.

map.Guaranteed returns on every fund: Active managers who pick winning stocks
map.No exposure to markets, cash only: Concentration in a few hot stocks

ww.Active managers who pick winning stocks: Index funds follow a market index rather than relying on managers picking stocks; their appeal is low fees and broad diversification for the long term.
ww.Concentration in a few hot stocks: Index funds hold many securities to spread risk, so concentrating in a few popular stocks is the opposite of their appeal.

map.A tax paid only by the poor and the midd: A tax where lower incomes face higher rates
map.A tax with no rate set by any law at all: A tax added to the price of goods sold
map.A tax with the same rate for every taxpa: A tax charged at one flat rate on income

ww.A tax where lower incomes face higher ra: Higher rates on lower incomes describe a regressive tax; a progressive tax raises the rate as income rises.
ww.A tax added to the price of goods sold: A tax added to purchases is a sales tax; a progressive tax is an income tax whose rates climb with higher income brackets.
ww.A tax charged at one flat rate on income: A single flat rate on income is a flat tax; a progressive tax uses higher rates for higher income brackets.

map.Only banks can see them, and not the per: Your employer gets a free copy and you do not
map.You must pay for every report that you r: You get your credit score free but pay for the reports

ww.Your employer gets a free copy and you d: Employers cannot freely view your credit report; the right belongs to you, so you can check your own reports from each major bureau for free.
ww.You get your credit score free but pay f: Federal law lets you get the reports themselves for free from each major bureau, so paying for them is not required.

map.A budget with no spending at all, so all: A budget that sets spending to zero so the whole paycheck goes to savings
map.A budget with zero savings, so every dol: A budget that begins each year with zero dollars in savings
map.A budget with no income, so the plan sho: A budget that lists the month's income and leaves the spending categories blank

ww.A budget that sets spending to zero so t: A zero-based budget assigns every dollar a job, including bills, fun and savings, so income minus planned spending is zero; it does not mean no spending.
ww.A budget that begins each year with zero: Zero-based refers to assigning all income until nothing is left unassigned, not to the starting savings balance, which can be any amount.
ww.A budget that lists the month's income a: A zero-based budget fills in every spending and saving category until the plan reaches zero; leaving categories blank leaves income unassigned.

map.Saving all money in one account so the b: Transferring money between your accounts using online banking
map.Using only credit cards for all of your: Putting each month's receipts into a labeled folder

ww.Transferring money between your accounts: Moving money between accounts online is a banking task; the envelope method divides physical cash into labeled envelopes by spending category.
ww.Putting each month's receipts into a lab: Filing receipts helps record keeping, but the envelope method limits spending by dividing actual cash into envelopes for each category.

map.To avoid saving any money at all later: To satisfy a tax filing requirement
map.Budgets never need changes once written: Prices and bills stay fixed for years

ww.To satisfy a tax filing requirement: No law requires a household budget to be reviewed for tax filing; the reason is that income, expenses and goals change over time.
ww.Prices and bills stay fixed for years: Prices, bills and income change, so a plan written once soon stops matching your life and must be reviewed and updated.

map.They are identical in every sense and bo: APR is quoted on credit cards while APY is quoted on car loans
map.APY applies to credit cards only, and ne: APY is the monthly rate while APR is the rate charged each year

ww.APR is quoted on credit cards while APY: Both APR and APY are annual figures; APR is the yearly cost of borrowing, while APY is the yearly yield on savings including compounding.
ww.APY is the monthly rate while APR is the: APY is not a monthly rate; it is an annual yield on savings that includes compounding, while APR is the yearly cost of borrowing.

map.Mailing cash to the bank in an envelope: Sending a check by mail to a branch for processing
map.Cashing at a store only, where the clerk: Handing a paper check to a teller at a branch

ww.Sending a check by mail to a branch for: Mailing a check is a paper process; mobile deposit uses a phone photo of the check so nothing needs to be sent or carried to a branch.
ww.Handing a paper check to a teller at a b: Handing a check to a teller is an in-person deposit; mobile check deposit lets you deposit through an app by photographing the check.

ww.Up to twenty years: Twenty years is far too long; most negative items fall off after about seven years, and even bankruptcies are limited to about ten years.
ww.Up to three months: Three months is much too short; late payments and collections generally remain on a credit report for several years.

ww.One report per two years: The bureaus currently offer free reports weekly at AnnualCreditReport.com, so waiting two years between reports is far less often than allowed.
ww.One report per five years: Five years is much rarer than what is offered; every consumer can get free reports from each bureau weekly through the official site.
ww.One report per three years: The bureaus now offer free reports weekly, so a three-year wait does not match current practice for AnnualCreditReport.com.

map.Unsecured loans are always cheaper than: Unsecured loans carry lower rates because the lender takes more risk
map.They are identical in every way and have: A secured loan has no interest while an unsecured loan charges interest

ww.Unsecured loans carry lower rates becaus: A lender taking more risk charges higher rates, not lower; unsecured loans usually cost more because there is no collateral to claim if the borrower defaults.
ww.A secured loan has no interest while an: Both kinds of loans charge interest; the difference is collateral, which backs a secured loan and is absent from an unsecured one.

map.None of it is taxed at the higher rate: Your income is averaged between the two rates
map.Only your savings are taxed at the highe: Your investment income moves to the higher rate

ww.Your income is averaged between the two: Tax brackets are not averaged; each slice of income is taxed at its own rate, and only the portion above the threshold gets the higher rate.
ww.Your investment income moves to the high: Brackets apply to taxable income as a whole, not to investment income alone; only the part above the bracket threshold is taxed at the higher rate.

map.Health coverage for illness and injury o: Coverage that pays medical bills for illness
map.No payout is ever made to anyone at any: Income replacement if the owner becomes disabled

ww.Coverage that pays medical bills for ill: Paying medical bills describes health insurance; whole life insurance pays a death benefit and builds cash value over the insured's lifetime.
ww.Income replacement if the owner becomes: Replacing income after a disability is what disability insurance does; whole life pays a death benefit to the beneficiary and builds cash value.

map.Only one month after you file them, no m: Six months after you file, then they can be shredded
map.They never need keeping, the agency has: Until you receive your refund, then discard them
map.Only one week after you file them, no mo: One year, since audits end after that

ww.Six months after you file, then they can: Six months is too short; the tax agency can audit returns for years, so documents should be kept at least three years and longer in some cases.
ww.Until you receive your refund, then disc: Receiving a refund does not end the audit window; you need your own records to support deductions if the agency asks questions years later.
ww.One year, since audits end after that: Audits and amended returns can happen after one year; the usual guidance is to keep returns and supporting documents at least three years.

map.Writing it on your phone case where anyo: Keeping it in a text file named passwords on your desktop
map.Using one simple password everywhere, ch: Using a favorite word with a number added at the end

ww.Keeping it in a text file named password: A plainly named text file is easy for malware or anyone with access to the computer to find, so it offers little protection for your accounts.
ww.Using a favorite word with a number adde: A word with a number added is easy to guess and often reused; a strong password is long and unique for each account.

map.Private loans always have lower rates th: Private loans offer income-driven repayment while federal loans depend on the lender
map.They are identical in every respect, wit: Federal loans are issued by colleges while private loans come from the government
map.Federal loans never need repayment, what: Federal loans are forgiven after graduation while private loans must be repaid

ww.Private loans offer income-driven repaym: This swaps the two; federal loans carry government protections like income-driven repayment, while private loans vary by lender.
ww.Federal loans are issued by colleges whi: Federal student loans are funded by the government and private loans come from banks and other lenders, so this description reverses who issues them.
ww.Federal loans are forgiven after graduat: Federal loans must be repaid; they may be deferred or forgiven only under specific programs, not simply because the borrower graduates.

map.Unlimited mileage on every trip you take: You pay for major repairs after the warranty ends
map.You always own the car, as the lease pas: You can sell the car to a buyer whenever you like
map.No monthly payments are required on a le: You must pay the full price of the car on signing day

ww.You pay for major repairs after the warr: Most leases are short enough to stay under warranty, so major repair bills are not the typical downside; the real drawbacks are no ownership and mileage limits.
ww.You can sell the car to a buyer whenever: A leased car belongs to the lessor, so you cannot sell it freely; lacking ownership is part of the downside of leasing.
ww.You must pay the full price of the car o: Leases usually need only a smaller upfront payment plus monthly payments; paying the full price on signing day describes a cash purchase.

map.An account only for the bank's own staff: An account held in the name of a business
map.An account open only to young children: An account that holds money for a minor child

ww.An account held in the name of a busines: An account held in a business name is a business account; a joint account is shared by two or more individuals who each have access.
ww.An account that holds money for a minor: An account holding money for a minor child is a custodial account; a joint account is owned by two or more people who share access.

map.An account for businesses only, managed: An account owned jointly by a married couple
map.An account the government opens for ever: An account opened by a school for a student

ww.An account owned jointly by a married co: An account owned by a couple is a joint account; a custodial account is run by an adult for the benefit of a minor.
ww.An account opened by a school for a stud: Schools do not open custodial accounts; an adult such as a parent sets one up and manages it until the child reaches the age of majority.

map.A permanent rate that never changes in t: A rate that stays low until the card is closed
map.A rate that applies only to cash advance: A rate set for customers who pay on time each month

ww.A rate that stays low until the card is: An introductory rate is temporary and ends after a set number of months, so a rate that stays low until closing does not describe it.
ww.A rate set for customers who pay on time: A reward for paying on time is not an introductory offer; an introductory 0 percent APR is a temporary rate offered when you open a new card.

map.Private loans are always forgiven after: Private loans are backed by the government and federal loans are not
map.Private loans always have lower interest: Federal loans require a credit check and a cosigner while private loans do not

ww.Private loans are backed by the governme: Federal loans are the ones backed by the government; private loans come from banks and other lenders without those protections.
ww.Federal loans require a credit check and: Many federal loans need no credit check or cosigner, while private lenders usually require both, so this description is backwards.

map.A free product that comes with every pai: A price that rises each year on a paid membership plan
map.A discount that never ends for customers: A coupon that expires if you do not use it in time

ww.A price that rises each year on a paid m: A yearly price increase is a pricing change, not a trap; a subscription trap starts as a free trial that quietly converts to paid billing.
ww.A coupon that expires if you do not use: An expiring coupon is a normal promotion; a subscription trap is a free trial that turns into recurring charges unless you cancel.

ww.Cheaper trades through an app: Cheap app-based trading is typical of a discount broker; a full-service broker charges more because it provides personal advice, research and planning.
ww.Access to online trading tools: Discount brokers also offer online trading tools, so this is not a difference; full-service brokers stand out for personalized advice and research.
ww.Insurance against market losses: Brokers do not insure clients against market losses; investments can fall in value, and a full-service broker adds advice and research instead.

map.Young drivers drive newer cars only, whi: Young drivers are required by law to buy extra coverage
map.Young drivers are never insured, as firm: Insurers raise rates on young drivers to match inflation
map.Young drivers always cause accidents on: Young drivers pay more because they drive fewer miles per year

ww.Young drivers are required by law to buy: No law forces young drivers to buy extra coverage; insurers charge more because statistics show less experienced drivers have more accidents.
ww.Insurers raise rates on young drivers to: Inflation affects all drivers equally; young drivers pay more because insurers price by risk and inexperienced drivers have more accidents.
ww.Young drivers pay more because they driv: Driving fewer miles would lower risk and premiums, not raise them; young drivers pay more because inexperience leads to more accidents.

map.It removes the need to budget at all: It makes keeping a budget unnecessary
map.It guarantees higher interest at banks: It raises your credit score right away

ww.It makes keeping a budget unnecessary: A budget is still needed to plan income and spending; a separate savings account is one tool that helps by making the money harder to spend.
ww.It raises your credit score right away: Opening a savings account does not change your credit score; the real benefit is that separation reduces the temptation to spend the money.

map.It removes the need for any bank account: It increases the interest rate on your account
map.It allows spending of saved money at any: It lets you skip paying your monthly bills
map.It earns the highest interest in the mar: It protects your savings from inflation

ww.It increases the interest rate on your a: Automatic transfers do not change the interest rate; they move money on a schedule so you save regularly without relying on willpower.
ww.It lets you skip paying your monthly bil: Automatic transfers move money into savings; they do not pay bills for you, and bills still need to be handled separately.
ww.It protects your savings from inflation: An automatic transfer is only a way of moving money and does not protect savings from inflation; it simply builds the habit of saving consistently.

map.Buying and selling every day to gain fro: Selling investments soon after a small gain
map.Buying only when prices fall and selling: Moving money into whichever fund did best last quarter

ww.Selling investments soon after a small g: Selling soon after a small gain is short-term trading; buy and hold means keeping investments for many years to ride out market ups and downs.
ww.Moving money into whichever fund did bes: Moving into last quarter's top fund is performance chasing; buy and hold keeps investments through ups and downs without frequent switching.

map.It can be opened only by retirees over s: It has an employer match on contributions
map.It has no contribution limits at all for: It must be opened through your employer

ww.It has an employer match on contribution: A Roth IRA is an individual account and has no employer match; people choose it mainly because qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free.
ww.It must be opened through your employer: A Roth IRA is opened by an individual at a brokerage or bank, not through an employer, and workers of any age with earned income may use one.

map.Your taxes drop on all of your income fo: Your earlier income is taxed at the average of both rates
map.All of your income is taxed at the highe: Your take-home pay falls below what you earned before the raise

ww.Your earlier income is taxed at the aver: Brackets are marginal, so earlier income stays at its lower rates and is not averaged with the higher one; only the income in the higher bracket gets the higher rate.
ww.Your take-home pay falls below what you: A raise never lowers take-home pay because only the extra income in the higher bracket is taxed more; you still keep part of every added dollar.

map.Short-term gains are never taxed at the: Long-term gains are deferred until the investor reaches age 65
map.Long-term gains are always tax-free, wha: Short-term gains are taxed twice, which raises their rate

ww.Long-term gains are deferred until the i: Long-term gains are taxed in the year the asset is sold, not deferred to a certain age; the lower rate rewards holding for more than a year.
ww.Short-term gains are taxed twice, which: Short-term gains are taxed once at ordinary income rates; they are not taxed twice, and the difference is that long-term gains get lower special rates.

map.When they have no receipts to claim at a: When their income is higher than average
map.When they have no expenses to claim at a: When they are filing for the first time

ww.When their income is higher than average: Itemizing depends on whether deductible expenses exceed the standard deduction, not on income level, so a high earner with few expenses should still take the standard deduction.
ww.When they are filing for the first time: Filing for the first time does not make itemizing better; the choice depends on whether allowed expenses add up to more than the standard deduction.

map.A rise in the price of one item only: A rise in the value of a currency
map.A rise in wages only, not prices: A rise in interest rates on loans

ww.A rise in the value of a currency: A rising currency value is appreciation, which makes money buy more; inflation is a general rise in prices that makes money buy less.
ww.A rise in interest rates on loans: Higher loan interest rates are a change in the cost of borrowing; inflation is a general rise in the price level across the economy.

map.It never changes in value, whatever happ: It earns a steady interest payment each month
map.It is invested in stocks and bonds only: It is held in real estate for many years

ww.It earns a steady interest payment each: Earning interest does not make money liquid; liquidity means how quickly an asset can be spent or turned into cash without losing much value.
ww.It is held in real estate for many years: Real estate takes time and effort to sell, so it is illiquid; liquid money can be spent or converted to cash quickly.

map.A fund that pays out all of its assets o: A fund that moves toward riskier stocks as a retirement date nears
map.A fund that buys stocks only on the last: A fund that pays a fixed income to retirees each month
map.A fund that invests only in companies ab: A fund that holds one mix of assets until its target date

ww.A fund that moves toward riskier stocks: This reverses the glide path; a target-date fund becomes more conservative, shifting toward bonds and cash as the retirement year gets closer.
ww.A fund that pays a fixed income to retir: A target-date fund is an investment fund that adjusts its mix over time; it does not promise a fixed monthly income to retirees.
ww.A fund that holds one mix of assets unti: A target-date fund changes its mix of stocks and bonds as the target year nears, so holding one unchanged mix does not describe it.

map.Top funds are always the safest choice f: Fees rise after a strong year
map.Top funds never charge any fees to their: Top funds hold too many stocks

ww.Fees rise after a strong year: Fund fees do not automatically rise after a good year; the risk of chasing winners is that past performance does not predict future results.
ww.Top funds hold too many stocks: Holding many stocks is a form of diversification, not a risk; chasing last year's winner is risky because strong past results often do not repeat.

map.Only government bonds and cash funds: Mostly Treasury bonds held to maturity
map.Only insured savings accounts at banks: Mostly CDs and money market funds

ww.Mostly Treasury bonds held to maturity: Mostly Treasury bonds held to maturity is a cautious, low-risk approach; an aggressive portfolio holds a high share of stocks seeking growth.
ww.Mostly CDs and money market funds: CDs and money market funds are safe and low-return, so a portfolio built from them is conservative rather than aggressive.

ww.Concentrate on winners: Concentrating on winners puts more eggs in one basket; the saying advises spreading money across different investments to reduce risk.
ww.Keep cash handy: Keeping cash handy is about liquidity; the eggs saying advises diversifying so that one poor performer cannot ruin the whole portfolio.

map.Tips are guaranteed by regulators, so no: Tips are reviewed by regulators before they are posted
map.Tips are always accurate and come from e: Tips come from licensed advisors who have studied the stock

ww.Tips are reviewed by regulators before t: Regulators do not review social media posts before publication, so tips can be false, paid promotions or part of a scheme.
ww.Tips come from licensed advisors who hav: Many tips come from anonymous accounts with no license or research and some have hidden interests, so acting on them without checking is risky.

map.Investing is the same as saving, with th: Saving seeks growth with risk while investing prioritizes safety and access
map.Saving always earns more than investing: Saving is done through a broker while investing is done at a bank

ww.Saving seeks growth with risk while inve: This swaps the two ideas; saving is for safety and easy access, while investing accepts risk in order to seek growth over a longer period.
ww.Saving is done through a broker while in: Saving usually happens in bank accounts and investing usually happens through a broker, so this reverses where each is done.

map.The 16 oz bottle because it costs less i: The 16 oz bottle, since $3.20 is the lower price
map.They are the same price per ounce in tot: Neither, since both cost about $0.19 an ounce

ww.The 16 oz bottle, since $3.20 is the low: The lower total price does not mean the better value; the smaller bottle costs $0.20 an ounce, while the 24 oz bottle costs about $0.175.
ww.Neither, since both cost about $0.19 an: The bottles do not cost the same per ounce; $3.20 divided by 16 is $0.20, while $4.20 divided by 24 is $0.175, so the larger bottle is cheaper.

map.Monthly payments are never important at: A lower payment means a cheaper loan
map.Lenders never charge any fees of any kin: Rates are set by the government for loans
map.Total cost is always equal to the monthl: Total cost is found by doubling the monthly payment

ww.A lower payment means a cheaper loan: A lower monthly payment often comes from a longer term, which adds interest, so the total cost can be higher even though each payment is smaller.
ww.Rates are set by the government for loan: Lenders set their own interest rates and fees, which vary widely, so comparing total cost is how you find the cheapest loan.
ww.Total cost is found by doubling the mont: Total cost is the sum of all payments plus fees over the full term, which is usually many times the monthly payment.

map.Only the price charts of the company's o: The past price patterns of a company's stock
map.Social media trends about the company's: Public mood about the brand on social media

ww.The past price patterns of a company's s: Studying past price patterns is technical analysis; fundamental analysis looks at the business itself, such as profits, debts and growth prospects.
ww.Public mood about the brand on social me: Public mood may influence prices, but fundamental analysis focuses on financial statements, earnings and business outlook rather than social media sentiment.

map.Dividends only, with no change in the pr: Price change minus the broker fees

ww.Dividends paid minus taxes owed: Dividends after tax is only part of the picture and leaves out price change; total return combines price change with dividends or interest.
ww.Price change minus the broker fees: Total return counts price change plus dividends or interest; subtracting fees gives a net figure but leaves out the income part of the return.

map.The number of investments an investor ow: How many years an investor plans to hold
map.How much an investor earns each year in: How much money an investor has available to invest

ww.How many years an investor plans to hold: The length of time an investor plans to hold is the time horizon; risk tolerance is about how much loss the investor can accept.
ww.How much money an investor has available: The money available to invest is capital; risk tolerance concerns comfort with possible losses, not the size of the investor's funds.

map.Only a short-term CD: A larger share of short-term CDs
map.Only cash under a mattress: A larger share of cash savings

ww.A larger share of short-term CDs: Short-term CDs are safe but earn little, which wastes a long time horizon and high risk tolerance that suit a larger share of stocks.
ww.A larger share of cash savings: Cash savings keep up poorly with inflation, so a young investor with a long horizon and high risk tolerance would favor more stocks.
ww.A single stock tip: Putting money in a single stock tip concentrates risk and is not reasonable; a larger share of diversified stocks suits a long horizon better.

map.Paying fees to a broker for each trade m: Choosing which brokerage will hold and manage your investment accounts
map.Selling all investments in a portfolio a: Moving a portfolio into whichever asset gained most this year

ww.Choosing which brokerage will hold and m: Picking a brokerage is a service choice; asset allocation divides the portfolio among asset classes such as stocks, bonds and cash.
ww.Moving a portfolio into whichever asset: Moving into last year's best asset is performance chasing; asset allocation sets a planned mix of stocks, bonds and cash based on goals.

map.Never changing the portfolio once it is: Switching to a new set of investments
map.Buying only the best performer of the ye: Adding more money to winning holdings

ww.Switching to a new set of investments: Switching to new investments replaces holdings; rebalancing keeps the same holdings but buys and sells to return to the target allocation.
ww.Adding more money to winning holdings: Adding to winners makes the portfolio drift further from its target; rebalancing trims what has grown too large and restores the planned mix.

ww.First claim on company assets: Bondholders and other creditors are paid before common stockholders, who are last in line, so common stock does not give first claim on assets.
ww.Repayment of principal at maturity: Repayment of principal at maturity is a feature of bonds; common stock represents ownership and has no maturity date.

map.It always pays a higher dividend than an: It pays variable dividends that rank after common dividends
map.It cannot be sold on any exchange or mar: It matures on a set date and repays its face value

ww.It pays variable dividends that rank aft: Preferred dividends are usually fixed and are paid before common dividends, not after, which is the feature that gives preferred stock its name.
ww.It matures on a set date and repays its: Preferred stock is a form of equity with no maturity date; repayment of face value at a set date is a feature of a bond.

map.The market where only bonds are traded b: The market where older securities are resold by one investor to another
map.The market where investors trade securit: The market where banks lend money to each other for short terms

ww.The market where older securities are re: Resale of older securities between investors happens in the secondary market; the primary market is where the issuer sells new securities for the first time.
ww.The market where banks lend money to eac: Short-term lending between banks is the money market; the primary market is where new securities are first sold by the issuer.

map.A stock that pays no attention to profit: A stock whose earnings are growing faster than the rest of the market
map.A stock with no assets, no profits and n: A stock that pays a high and steady dividend to its holders

ww.A stock whose earnings are growing faste: A stock with rapidly growing earnings is a growth stock; a value stock appears cheap relative to fundamentals such as earnings or assets.
ww.A stock that pays a high and steady divi: A stock known for high, steady dividends is an income stock; a value stock is defined by a low price relative to its fundamentals.

map.A stock issued only by banks and insurer: A stock that trades at a low price relative to earnings
map.A stock that falls every year by design: A stock of a young company expected to grow fast

ww.A stock that trades at a low price relat: A stock priced low relative to earnings is a value stock; an income stock is defined by relatively high, steady dividends paid to holders.
ww.A stock of a young company expected to g: A stock of a fast-growing young company is a growth stock; an income stock pays relatively high, steady dividends.

map.Only on weekends and public holidays eac: 4:00 p.m. to 9:30 a.m. Eastern on business days
map.24 hours every day of the year, with no: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern on business days

ww.4:00 p.m. to 9:30 a.m. Eastern on busine: Those hours are when the regular session is closed; regular U.S. trading runs from 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern on business days.
ww.9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern on busine: Regular U.S. sessions open at 9:30 a.m. and close at 4:00 p.m. Eastern, not the standard office hours of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

map.Trading only with cash on hand and no lo: Buying shares with a tax-free retirement account
map.Trading only on the edges of a market, n: Trading shares in foreign companies on overseas exchanges

ww.Buying shares with a tax-free retirement: Buying through a retirement account is about account type; margin trading means borrowing from a broker to buy securities with the account as collateral.
ww.Trading shares in foreign companies on o: Trading foreign shares on overseas exchanges is international investing; margin is about borrowing money from a broker, not about where shares trade.

map.They always move the same way: They move in the same direction

ww.They move in the same direction: Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions; when a price rises the fixed coupon is a smaller percent of it, so the yield falls.
ww.They stay fixed after issue: The price of a bond changes with market conditions after issue, and its yield changes with it, so neither stays fixed.

map.The company cannot be sold to anyone at: The stock is overvalued compared with its assets
map.The company has no assets left to sell a: The stock must be delisted from its exchange by law

ww.The stock is overvalued compared with it: A price below book value means the market values the company at less than its recorded net assets, which suggests it is undervalued or has problems, not overvalued.
ww.The stock must be delisted from its exch: No law requires delisting because a stock trades below book value; exchanges delist for other reasons, and the price may signal undervaluation or trouble.

map.It always matches the market exactly eac: It pays a dividend 1.5 times the market average
map.It never moves up or down in price at al: It costs 1.5 times as much as the average stock

ww.It pays a dividend 1.5 times the market: Beta measures how much a stock's price moves relative to the market, not the size of its dividend; 1.5 means it tends to move more than the market.
ww.It costs 1.5 times as much as the averag: Beta says nothing about a share's price level; it measures sensitivity to market moves, so 1.5 means larger swings than the market.

map.A bond that pays interest every single m: A bond that pays interest twice a year
map.A bond that never repays the face value: A bond that repays half its face value

ww.A bond that pays interest twice a year: Paying interest twice a year describes a typical coupon bond; a zero-coupon bond pays no periodic interest and is sold at a discount to face value.
ww.A bond that repays half its face value: A zero-coupon bond repays its full face value at maturity, and the gap between the discounted price and face value is the investor's return.

map.A fund that never changes its holdings a: A fund that is closed to new investors after launch
map.A fund that holds one stock only at a ti: A fund that buys real estate and rents it to tenants

ww.A fund that is closed to new investors a: Closing a fund to new investors is a separate matter; a passive fund tracks an index with little trading to keep costs low.
ww.A fund that buys real estate and rents i: Buying and renting real estate describes a property investment trust; a passive fund holds the many securities of the index it tracks.

map.A CD always pays more than a bond, as ba: A CD is issued by the Treasury; a bond is issued by banks
map.A CD cannot earn any interest at all in: A CD gives ownership in a bank; a bond gives ownership in a firm

ww.A CD is issued by the Treasury; a bond i: CDs are issued by banks and credit unions, while bonds are issued by governments and corporations, so this swaps the issuers.
ww.A CD gives ownership in a bank; a bond g: A bond is debt, not ownership, and a CD is a deposit, so neither gives a stake in a company or a bank.

map.A fund that never changes its mix of hol: A fund that is run by a bank and insured by the FDIC
map.A fund that is open only to employees of: A fund that pays a fixed return set by its sponsor

ww.A fund that is run by a bank and insured: Mutual funds are not FDIC insured and can lose value; an open-end fund is defined by continually issuing and redeeming shares at net asset value.
ww.A fund that pays a fixed return set by i: Mutual funds do not promise a set return; their value follows the investments they hold, and open-end refers to share issuance and redemption.

map.A fund that never changes its holdings a: A fund that automatically adds more stocks and fewer bonds as a retirement date approaches
map.A fund that invests only in one company: A fund that holds bonds maturing in the same year as the target date

ww.A fund that automatically adds more stoc: This reverses the pattern; a target-date fund becomes more conservative, moving toward bonds as the retirement date gets closer to lower risk.
ww.A fund that holds bonds maturing in the: Holding bonds that mature in one year describes a target-maturity bond fund; a target-date fund holds stocks and bonds and shifts the mix over time.

map.A fund holding only stocks and no bonds: A fund holding a mix of real estate and gold
map.A fund holding only cash and no stocks a: A fund holding shares of companies from many countries

ww.A fund holding a mix of real estate and: A mix of real estate and gold describes an alternative or commodity fund; a balanced fund holds a set mix of stocks and bonds.
ww.A fund holding shares of companies from: Holding shares from many countries describes an international fund; a balanced fund blends stocks and bonds to balance growth and income.

map.A fund that pays in foreign currency onl: A fund that invests in companies with a global brand name
map.A fund that invests only in U.S. compani: A fund that invests in the largest companies in the home market

ww.A fund that invests in companies with a: A global brand name does not make a fund international; many such companies are based at home, and an international fund invests in firms outside the home country.
ww.A fund that invests in the largest compa: Investing in the largest home companies is a large-cap domestic fund; an international fund invests in companies outside the investor's home country.

map.A firm that only lends to homebuyers: A firm that makes mortgage loans to homebuyers
map.A firm that only sells insurance policie: A firm that manages tax returns for clients
map.A firm that only prints money for the st: A firm that issues credit cards to consumers

ww.A firm that makes mortgage loans to home: Making mortgage loans is the work of a lender; a broker-dealer works in securities, trading as an agent for clients and for its own account.
ww.A firm that manages tax returns for clie: Preparing tax returns is an accounting service; a broker-dealer trades securities for clients and for its own account.
ww.A firm that issues credit cards to consu: Issuing credit cards is a consumer lending business; a broker-dealer is a securities firm that trades for clients and for itself.

map.A broker that only executes orders, givi: A broker offering low fees and online trades
map.A broker that does not trade for clients: A broker who sells one fund family's products

ww.A broker offering low fees and online tr: Low fees and online trades describe a discount broker; a full-service broker adds advice, research and planning, usually for higher fees.
ww.A broker who sells one fund family's pro: Selling one fund family's products describes a captive agent; a full-service broker offers advice, research and planning along with trade execution.

map.Clients must buy only the cheapest produ: Brokers must recommend the product with the highest return
map.Clients cannot ask questions of their br: Clients must hold investments for at least one year

ww.Brokers must recommend the product with: Suitability does not require recommending the highest-return product, which is often the riskiest; recommendations must fit the client's goals and risk tolerance.
ww.Clients must hold investments for at lea: Suitability sets no holding period for clients; it requires that recommendations match the client's goals, finances and risk tolerance.

map.A person who must maximize their own pro: A person required to beat the market for each client
map.A person who works only for commissions: A person who holds a client's money in a personal account

ww.A person required to beat the market for: A fiduciary must act in the client's best interest, but cannot be required to beat the market, because no adviser can promise that.
ww.A person who holds a client's money in a: Mixing client money into a personal account breaches a fiduciary's duty; a fiduciary must put the client's interest first and avoid conflicts.

map.Buying only government bonds, the safest: Accepting less risk for steady income
map.Avoiding all risk in every investment yo: Holding investments for as long as possible

ww.Accepting less risk for steady income: Accepting less risk for steady income describes a conservative investor; an aggressive investor accepts more risk in pursuit of higher potential returns.
ww.Holding investments for as long as possi: Holding period alone does not make someone aggressive; the term describes accepting more risk and volatility for the chance of higher returns.

map.It removes all risk of loss entirely: It lowers fees by buying in bulk
map.It guarantees profits in every year: It lets you avoid paying taxes on gains

ww.It lowers fees by buying in bulk: Diversification does not lower fees; it spreads money so weak results in one area may be offset by stronger results in another.
ww.It lets you avoid paying taxes on gains: Diversification has no effect on tax owed; its benefit is that weak results in one area may be offset by others.

map.One company's stock only, held alone: Shares of one company held in two accounts
map.Ten bonds from the same issuer only: Bonds from the same issuer with different maturities

ww.Shares of one company held in two accoun: Holding the same company in two accounts is still one company's risk; a diversified portfolio spreads money across asset classes and many firms.
ww.Bonds from the same issuer with differen: Different maturities from one issuer still depend on that issuer's ability to pay, so this is not diversified across firms or asset classes.

map.Only recent days matter to most investor: Future returns will be lower than past returns
map.Investments never lose any value at all: Losses from the past cannot happen again

ww.Future returns will be lower than past r: The phrase does not predict lower returns; it warns that past returns do not promise any particular result, which could be higher or lower.
ww.Losses from the past cannot happen again: Past losses can happen again; the phrase warns that history does not promise what comes next, and markets can fall as well as rise.

map.Higher fees always mean higher returns o: Higher fees pay for better long-term performance
map.Fees do not affect returns at all for in: Fees are paid by the fund company, not investors

ww.Higher fees pay for better long-term per: Higher fees do not reliably buy better performance; many costly funds trail cheaper ones, and fees reduce what the investor keeps.
ww.Fees are paid by the fund company, not i: Fund fees are taken out of the fund's assets, so investors bear them through lower returns, which is why comparing fees matters.

map.Leaving the portfolio untouched forever,: Switching your portfolio to new investments
map.Buying only the winners of the past year: Putting more money into last year's winners

ww.Switching your portfolio to new investme: Switching to new investments replaces holdings, while rebalancing adjusts existing holdings back to target weights after market moves.
ww.Putting more money into last year's winn: Putting more money into last year's winners is performance chasing, which moves the portfolio away from target weights instead of back toward them.
